entries.test: Whether frontier-model benchmark gains per added unit of training compute and data were clearly shrinking around early 2025, compared with earlier generations.
entries.note: "Diminishing results" is taken to mean diminishing returns from scaling. The measure is loose, but most readers would test it this way.

entries.test: Whether Llama 4's released models score clearly below GPT-5 (released August 2025) on standard benchmarks and evaluations.
entries.note: Marcus himself hedges the threshold as "what we might call GPT-5 level", so the bar is vague.

entries.test: Whether any model from OpenAI, xAI, Google or Anthropic released before April 7, 2025 matched GPT-5-level benchmark performance.
entries.note: The claim describes the state of things on April 7, 2025. Without that date the proposition could be read as current, when OpenAI has since shipped GPT-5.

entries.test: Whether Llama 4 performed well below what its training compute and data scale would have predicted, as shown by benchmarks and reporting on its development.
entries.note: "Waste" is evaluative. The testable core is that Llama 4 underperformed relative to its scale.

entries.test: Reactions to Llama 4 from researchers and developers in April 2025, in reviews, forums and coverage of the LMArena controversy.
entries.note: The proposition drops the hedge "pretty", which is a minor loss.
The proposition leaves out the named pundits (Roose, Newton, Cowen) and misstates benchmark juicing as part of the pundits' failure. Readers would also disagree on what "failing to reckon" means.
This is a truism used as a warning, and it commits to nothing testable.

entries.test: Surveys of customer satisfaction with generative AI from early 2025, and whether the named pundits' coverage discussed customer disappointment.
entries.note: This is two claims in one. "By pundits" comes from the surrounding context.
It is unclear whose expectations he means, and the second half is hedged with "appear". Readers would test it in different ways.
